verdict.rationale: Docs strongly support strict typing (generic Agent[Foobar, list[str]] types checked by IDE) and schema-validated structured outputs via Pydantic models forcing responses to match a spec, which underlies 'catch mistakes at build time'. However, independent hands-on reports describe structured-output validation actually failing or being unreliable in practice ('something was broken... difficult to figure out if it's the abstraction or the underlying LLM provider library' and 'vanilla pydantic-ai rarely [creates objects successfully], regardless of retries'), directly contradicting the reliability of the schema-validation claim. missing for 10: independent confirmation that build-time/static type checks reliably prevent agent errors, and resolution of the reported structured-output validation failures.
